high.title: Presidential Office Signals FX Market Management Intent Ahead of US Investment, Says 'Exchange Rate Must Stabilize'
high.summary: The Korean Presidential Office has publicly emphasized the need for exchange rate stability as the USD-KRW continues to rise, signaling potential government intervention concerns. A senior official accompanying President Lee's Italy visit stated that "the exchange rate needs to stabilize" and highlighted that the US Treasury Department "has a very deep understanding of our country's situation and is constantly monitoring it." The official emphasized the importance of exchange rate movements aligning with economic fundamentals. This represents a clear policy signal that Korean authorities are closely watching FX market developments and may be preparing intervention measures if volatility persists. For KRW traders, this suggests official resistance levels may emerge if USD-KRW continues climbing, while bond investors should monitor for potential policy responses that could impact yields.

high.title: 'National Pension Rebalancing Exemption Intensified Currency Pressure' - Welfare Ministry 'Disagrees with Causality' (Comprehensive)
high.summary: Barclays analysis suggests that the National Pension Service's suspension of portfolio rebalancing in H1 2026 acted as an "amplifier rather than stabilizer" in FX market volatility, indirectly triggering massive foreign capital outflows. The NPS halted rebalancing in January to support domestic markets during simultaneous stock and won weakness, raising domestic equity allocation from 14.4% to 14.9%, then further to 20.8% by May. While this boosted NPS returns, Barclays economist Bum-ki Son argues it amplified market volatility by disrupting normal capital flow patterns. This analysis is crucial for understanding recent KRW weakness drivers beyond typical economic fundamentals. Foreign investors may have been forced to rebalance elsewhere due to reduced NPS activity, creating additional selling pressure on Korean assets and the won.

high.title: NDF at 1,517.20/1,517.60 Won - Down 1.05 Won
high.summary: The USD-KRW one-month NDF declined in New York trading, quoted at 1,517.40 won (mid-rate), representing a 1.05 won decline from Seoul's previous closing of 1,519.80 won. The offshore rate suggests expectations for KRW strengthening, with the bid-ask spread at 1,517.20-1,517.60 won. The slight USD strength was attributed to ceasefire negotiation expectations and noise surrounding US-Iran talks. The NDF discount to spot rates indicates overseas markets are pricing in KRW recovery, potentially reflecting reduced geopolitical risk premiums if Middle East tensions ease.

medium.title: [FX-Weekly] Hormuz Opening, Foreign Rebalancing Inflection Point in Focus - Kevin Warsh's Debut Also Watched
medium.summary: The USD-KRW exchange rate is expected to test support in the early 1,500 won range this week as dollar weakness factors dominate amid ceasefire expectations between the US and Iran. Foreign investor remittance demand may reach an inflection point, potentially intensifying downward pressure on USD-KRW. Kevin Warsh's first FOMC meeting as Fed Chairman is also being closely watched for policy signals.

medium.title: [Bond Market - Weekly] Growing Expectations for War's End - Focus on Kevin Warsh's 'Debut'
medium.summary: Seoul's bond market will digest US-Iran ceasefire negotiation progress and the Fed's FOMC meeting this week. Strong ceasefire expectations emerged after Iran's Supreme Leader reportedly approved a ceasefire MOU, with Pakistani PM suggesting a final agreement within 24 hours. This could significantly impact risk sentiment and bond yields as geopolitical premiums unwind.

medium.title: South Korea Growth Outlook Rises to 3.7% - Will Government Forecast Break 3%?
medium.summary: Economic growth expectations are rising rapidly due to stronger-than-anticipated semiconductor-led export boom. Attention focuses on whether the government will raise its growth forecast to the 3% range this year, which could impact monetary policy expectations and bond yields as stronger growth may support hawkish BOK policy stances.

medium.title: Expanded Economy Fuels 'Proactive Fiscal' Push - Next Year's Budget to Exceed 800 Trillion Won
medium.summary: South Korea's government gains momentum for "proactive fiscal" stance as surging nominal GDP from the semiconductor supercycle boosts the economic weight class. Expanded nominal GDP increases tax revenue and reduces fiscal soundness concerns, providing justification for expansionary fiscal policies that could impact government bond supply and yields.
